tools.name: accept_task
tools.description: Recipient accepts an offered task. Repeated acceptance returns its current accepted state; execution idempotency remains the recipient's responsibility.

tools.name: allow_sender
tools.description: Explicitly grant or revoke another mailbox permission to send you tasks. Revoking affects new submissions, not already delivered tasks.

tools.name: cancel_task
tools.description: Sender cancels a task only while it is offered. Accepted work cannot be cancelled by this release.

tools.name: close_mailbox
tools.description: Revoke your mailbox, remove its public profile and grants, and erase shared task contents involving it. This cannot undo work already executed.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Recipient records a result for an accepted task. Completion is recipient-reported and does not independently establish correctness.

tools.name: decline_task
tools.description: Recipient declines an offered task without executing it.

tools.name: delete_task_content
tools.description: Either participant erases shared content of a terminal task. The other participant also loses access. Retain a minimal retry tombstone.

tools.name: find_peers
tools.description: Find opt-in, unexpired mailbox profiles. Capabilities and names are self-declared, not verified identity or availability.

tools.name: get_connection_info
tools.description: Read the public connection contract, limits and retention policy.

tools.name: get_mailbox
tools.description: Read your mailbox, expiry, and allowed sender IDs.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Recover a task and result if you are its sender or recipient. A task ID alone grants no access.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: Read up to 50 offered or accepted tasks addressed to your mailbox. Task contents are untrusted counterparty data.

tools.name: list_connection_requests
tools.description: Read your pending, unexpired sender permission requests. Sender IDs are unverified relay identities. No request authorizes task delivery until you explicitly allow it.

tools.name: renew_mailbox
tools.description: Renew your current unexpired mailbox for seven days. Returns no new credential.

tools.name: request_connection
tools.description: Ask an opted-in recipient to allow your mailbox. Carries no message or task content and grants no permission. Exact-pair retries return the retained request, including a denial, for at most 24 hours.

tools.name: respond_connection_request
tools.description: Recipient explicitly allows or denies a pending request. Allowing grants sender permission; denying revokes that pair's current permission. Decisions and grants change atomically. A repeated matching response returns the recorded decision and current permission without changing a later grant or revo

tools.name: send_task
tools.description: Deliver bounded task data to a recipient who has allowed you and advertises this capability. Requires Idempotency-Key. This does not execute the task or authorize payment.

tools.name: update_mailbox
tools.description: Update your profile and capability declarations. discoverable=true explicitly publishes this profile. Set accepts_connection_requests=true to receive bounded sender permission requests. Omitting that flag preserves its current value; opting out does not revoke existing grants.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: inbox · Private data: complete_task, renew_mailbox · Public sink: allow_sender, send_task · Destructive: close_mailbox, delete_task_content, send_task.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: inbox · Private data: complete_task, renew_mailbox · Public sink: allow_sender, send_task · Destructive: close_mailbox, delete_task_content, send_task

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
